questions.stem: Explain why water is important to a plant, giving three separate uses, and state which of them stops first when the plant is not watered.

fuzzyTraps.precise: water is needed for photosynthesis, for support, and to carry mineral salts

chain.text: Water is a raw material for photosynthesis.
Water in the cells keeps them firm, supporting the plant.
Mineral salts are transported around the plant dissolved in water.
Support fails first, which is why wilting is the first sign of a plant needing water.

questions.modelAnswer: Water is one of the raw materials the plant needs for photosynthesis, in which it makes its food. Water inside the cells also keeps them firm, which supports the plant and keeps the stem and leaves upright. In addition, the mineral salts absorbed from the soil are dissolved in water and transported in it to all parts of the plant. When a plant is not watered, the support function fails first: the cells lose water and are no longer firm enough to hold the leaves up, which is why wilting is the earliest visible sign that a plant needs water.
markPoints: Water is a raw material for photosynthesis
Water keeps the cells firm, supporting the plant
Water transports dissolved mineral salts around the plant
Support fails first, which is why wilting is the first visible sign
questions.whyMarksLost: Three marks means three distinct uses, and most answers give photosynthesis and stop. The fourth connects the science to what you actually see.

questions.commandDemand: Offer a workable method and explain how it reduces water loss.
questions.stimulus: A gardener moves a plant from the ground into a pot. For the next few days the plant wilts in the afternoon sun.
questions.stem: Suggest one thing the gardener could do to help the plant, explain how it would work, and state why the plant wilts only in the afternoon.

fuzzyTraps.vague: keep it out of the sun
fuzzyTraps.precise: place it in the shade, which reduces the rate of transpiration

chain.text: Move the plant into the shade during the hottest part of the day.
Less heat energy means a lower rate of transpiration and less water lost.
The afternoon sun is hottest, so transpiration peaks then and the plant wilts.

questions.modelAnswer: The gardener could move the plant into the shade during the hottest part of the day. In the shade the leaves receive less heat energy, which reduces the rate of transpiration and so reduces the water lost from the leaves, allowing the damaged roots to absorb enough to replace it so the cells stay firm. The plant wilts only in the afternoon because that is when the sun is hottest and the rate of transpiration is at its highest, so water is being lost faster than the roots can replace it at that time of day.
markPoints: A workable action such as moving it into the shade or watering it
Explained as reducing transpiration so water loss does not exceed absorption
The afternoon is hottest, so the rate of transpiration is highest then
questions.whyMarksLost: The timing mark links the symptom to the rate of transpiration, which is the idea the whole topic turns on.

questions.commandDemand: Offer a method that would make the transport visible, and say what would be seen.
questions.stimulus: A teacher wants to show her class the path taken by water inside the stem of a plant.
questions.stem: Suggest how she could do this, and state what the class would observe.

fuzzyTraps.precise: place the cut stem of a white flower in coloured water and leave it for several hours

chain.text: Place the cut stem of a white flower or celery stalk into coloured water.
Leave it for several hours so the water is transported up the stem.
Cut the stem across and see coloured dots where the water carrying tubes are, and coloured petals.

questions.modelAnswer: She could place the cut stem of a white flower, or a stick of celery, into a beaker of coloured water and leave it for several hours. The plant absorbs the coloured water and transports it up the stem. The class would then observe that the petals or the top of the stalk have turned that colour, and if the stem is cut across they would see coloured dots or lines showing exactly where the water carrying tubes are.
markPoints: Method: place a cut stem in coloured water and leave it for several hours
Observation stated: coloured petals, or coloured dots in the cut stem showing the water carrying tubes
questions.whyMarksLost: The observation is half the answer. Describing the setup without saying what would be seen leaves the second mark unclaimed.
